PLAN YOUR REQUIREMENT

A useful brief.
A clearer next step.

Frames, supports, enclosures and custom fabricated assemblies.

Decisions to make early

Share the assembly geometry, material grades and joint requirements. Identify distortion-sensitive dimensions, access restrictions and the final surface finish.

What to agree before work begins

Agree assembly drawings, weld requirements, inspection criteria and any applicable project-specific procedure or documentation requirements.

BEFORE YOU ENQUIRE

Questions,
answered.

What should a fabrication drawing show?+

Include overall dimensions, member or sheet sizes, material grades, joint details and critical interfaces. Add assembly references where the part connects to other equipment or furniture.

How should inspection requirements be specified?+

State the intended application and required acceptance criteria in the brief. Any project-specific testing, procedure qualification or documentation needs must be reviewed and agreed explicitly.

A CLEAR START

What to share.

Assembly drawings, material, joint requirements and expected use.

Technical scope, material suitability, tolerances, inspection criteria, pricing and timing are confirmed after reviewing your requirements.

A CONNECTED APPROACH

Think beyond
one process.

Your project may need design, fabrication, finishing and assembly together. Include the complete requirement so each step can be considered in context.
